# Weil cone and PBAP in the Lean corpus

Status on 7 October 2026. This report distinguishes unconditional theorems, implications with open hypotheses, excluded constructions, and problems still open in the searched corpus.

**The corpus proves the existence reformulation and many strong rigidity theorems. It does not supply an unconditional integer-supported Weil-positive system, an unconditional proof of PBAP, or a general implication from mere existence to RH.** The remaining gap is mathematical, not just an unformalized compactness or spectral-representation argument.

## Exact objects and logical status

Write \(\Lambda\) for the von Mangoldt function and \(\lambda:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R\). Values at 0 and 1 are irrelevant to the Weil functional; equality statements generally concern \(n\ge2\).

Two different positivity predicates occur:

- `RHTower.WeilPositive`: positivity at every aperture on compactly supported \(C^2\) tests whose Fourier transforms vanish at both polar points \(\pm i/2\).
- `RHTower.WeilPositiveFull`: positivity on **all** compactly supported \(C^2\) autocorrelation tests, retaining the pole term.

Neither definition requires \(\lambda(n)\ge0\). “Weil-positive” describes the quadratic form, not the signs of its coefficients. The full predicate implies the polar predicate. This audit did not locate a converse for arbitrary weights; the two versions must not be interchanged.

For the full cone, set \(\mathcal W=\{\lambda:\operatorname{WeilPositiveFull}(\lambda)\}\). In the corpus's normalization,

\[
Q_\lambda(f)=A_{\rm full}(f)-\sum_{n\ge2}\lambda(n)L_n(f),
\]

where \(A_{\rm full}\) contains the archimedean **and pole** contributions and \(L_n\) is the real symmetric autocorrelation value at \(\pm\log n\), divided by \(\sqrt n\). Each individual compactly supported test sees finitely many integers.

Full PBAP says: every finite nonnegative combination of tests with \(\sum_i\alpha_iL_n(f_i)=0\) for **every integer** \(n\ge2\) has nonnegative combined \(A_{\rm full}\). It is not blindness only at primes, and the underlying test functions need not be nonnegative.

| Statement | Corpus status |
|---|---|
| \(\mathrm{RH}\iff\Lambda\in\mathcal W\) | Proved. [Full Weil criterion](/Users/michael/Documents/code/hgt/formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/WeilFullConeExposedPoint.lean:569). |
| Full PBAP \(\iff\mathcal W\ne\varnothing\) | Proved. [Full duality](/Users/michael/Documents/code/hgt/formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/WeilFullConeOneSidedCriterion.lean:451). |
| \(\mathrm{RH}\Rightarrow\) full PBAP | Proved. [Forward implication](/Users/michael/Documents/code/hgt/formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/WeilFullConeOneSidedCriterion.lean:475). |
| Polar PBAP at every level \(\iff\exists\lambda\), `WeilPositive λ` | Proved separately. [Polar duality](/Users/michael/Documents/code/hgt/formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/WeilPositivityPrimeBlindDuality.lean:558). |
| Full or all-level polar PBAP, without an RH/positivity premise | No proof located. |
| \(\mathcal W\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow\mathrm{RH}\) | No general proof located. Additional sufficient conditions are proved below. |

Thus the proved existence equivalence must not be reported as an RH equivalence. Nor has the corpus established a counterexample to general detection.

## What has been proved beyond the reformulation

### Compactness and the finite to infinite passage

For polar positivity, existence at every finite aperture implies existence of one system positive at all apertures. The weights may depend on the aperture before taking the compactness limit. [Finite-level existence theorem](/Users/michael/Documents/code/hgt/formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/WeilPositivityFiniteLevelExistence.lean:119).

For full positivity, the normalized cone \(\lambda(0)=\lambda(1)=0\) is compact in the product topology. More sharply,

\[
\mathrm{RH}\iff\forall N\;\exists\lambda\in\mathcal W\quad
\lambda(n)=\Lambda(n)\quad(2\le n\le N).
\]

/-!
# Removing primes destroys Weil positivity

For a set `R` of primes, let `Λ_R(n) = Λ(n)` unless `n` is a power of a prime in `R`, and

many Euler factors does not move the zeros of `ζ` in the critical strip (the new zeros lie on
`Re s = 0`), but it destroys Weil positivity for the archimedean datum of `ζ`, unconditionally:
`Λ_R ≤ Λ`, and a full-cone Weil-positive minorant of `Λ` equals `Λ`
(`eq_vonMangoldt_of_weilPositiveFull_of_le`).

namespace RHTower
namespace RemovedPrimes

open ArithmeticFunction

/-- The von Mangoldt function with the powers of the primes in `R` removed. -/
noncomputable def vonMangoldtWithout (R : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  Set.indicator {m | ¬ ∃ p ∈ R, ∃ k, m = p ^ k} (fun m => (vonMangoldt m : ℝ)) n

theorem vonMangoldtWithout_le (R : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
    vonMangoldtWithout R n ≤ (vonMangoldt n : ℝ) :=
  Set.indicator_le_self' (fun _ _ => vonMangoldt_nonneg) n

/-- **Removing any prime destroys Weil positivity.**  If `R` contains a prime, then the von Mangoldt
function with the powers of the primes of `R` removed is not full-cone Weil-positive. -/
theorem not_weilPositiveFull_vonMangoldtWithout {R : Set ℕ} {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hpR : p ∈ R) :
    ¬ WeilPositiveFull (vonMangoldtWithout R) := by
  intro hW
  have h := eq_vonMangoldt_of_weilPositiveFull_of_le hW fun n _ => vonMangoldtWithout_le R n
  have hp2 := h p hp.two_le
  have hmem : p ∉ {m : ℕ | ¬ ∃ q ∈ R, ∃ k, m = q ^ k} := by
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, not_not]
    exact ⟨p, hpR, 1, (pow_one p).symm⟩
  have h0 : vonMangoldtWithout R p = 0 := Set.indicator_of_notMem hmem _
  rw [h0, vonMangoldt_apply_prime hp] at hp2
  exact (Real.log_pos (by exact_mod_cast hp.one_lt)).ne' hp2.symm

/-- In particular, the von Mangoldt function of `(1 - 2^{-s}) ζ(s)` (the prime `2` removed) is not
full-cone Weil-positive. -/
theorem not_weilPositiveFull_without_two :

/-!
# The vanishing criterion of a Siegel-type count

Assembling the geometry: a subgroup with compact quotient supplies a compact fundamental set and,
for any prescribed radius, a finite set of centres covering it.  Once the Schwarz gain
`(r/R)^N/(1−r/R)` is below one, *any* periodic function whose jets of order below `N` vanish at
every one of those centres is identically zero.

This is exactly the shape a dimension count consumes: the count produces the jet vanishing at a
finite prescribed set of points, and this theorem converts it into a global identity.

* **`exists_finite_centres_forcing_vanishing`**.
-/

open Set

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- **Finitely many centres whose jet vanishing forces a periodic function to vanish.** -/
theorem exists_finite_centres_forcing_vanishing
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    {P : AddSubgroup E} (hcpt : CompactSpace (E ⧸ P))
    {r R : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hrR : r < R) (hR : 0 < R) {N : ℕ}
    (hθ : (r / R) ^ N / (1 - r / R) < 1) :
    ∃ s : Set E, s.Finite ∧ ∀ F : E → ℂ, ContDiff ℂ (⊤ : ℕ∞) F →
      (∀ p ∈ P, ∀ z : E, F (z + p) = F z) →
      (∀ c ∈ s, ∀ k, k < N → iteratedFDeriv ℂ k F c = 0) → ∀ z, F z = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨K, s, hKcomp, hKne, hfund, hsfin, hcov⟩ :=
    exists_finite_centres_of_compactSpace_quotient hcpt hr
  refine ⟨s, hsfin, ?_⟩
  intro F hF hper hvan
  refine eqOn_zero_of_periodic_cover hF hper hKcomp hKne hfund
    (fun i : s => (i : E)) hr.le hrR hR ?_ ?_ hθ
  · intro i k hk
    exact hvan (i : E) i.2 k hk
  · intro z hz
    obtain ⟨c, hc, hzc⟩ := hcov z hz
    exact ⟨⟨c, hc⟩, hzc⟩

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-!
# Finite affine cyclic moment-symmetry universality

For an `n`-point complex multiset and a primitive `d`th root `ζ`, invariance under scalar
rotation by `ζ` is equivalent to vanishing of precisely the first `n` power sums lying outside
the trivial cyclic-character sector.  Translating the spectrum gives the corresponding sharp
criterion for rotation about an arbitrary center.

The order-two case recovers the odd-moment reflection criterion, while the statement and its
finite threshold are uniform in the cyclic order.
-/

open scoped BigOperators
open Finset

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

noncomputable section

/-- **Finite cyclic character criterion.**  An `n`-point spectrum is fixed by multiplication by
a primitive `d`th root exactly when all of its nontrivial-character power sums through order `n`
vanish. -/
theorem finiteCyclicScaling_fixed_iff_firstCharacterMoments_vanish
    {n d : ℕ} (f : Fin n → ℂ) {ζ : ℂ} (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ d) :
    (univ.val.map f).map (fun z => ζ * z) = univ.val.map f ↔
      ∀ k, k ≤ n → ¬ d ∣ k → ∑ i, f i ^ k = 0 := by
  rw [finiteMultiset_map_fixed_iff_firstPowerSums_fixed]
  constructor
  · intro h k hk hdk
    have heq := h k hk
    rw [← Finset.sum_eq_multiset_sum Finset.univ,
      ← Finset.sum_eq_multiset_sum Finset.univ] at heq
    simp_rw [mul_pow] at heq
    rw [← Finset.mul_sum] at heq
    have hne : ζ ^ k ≠ 1 := fun hone =>
      hdk ((hζ.pow_eq_one_iff_dvd k).mp hone)
    have hzero : (ζ ^ k - 1) * ∑ i, f i ^ k = 0 := by
      linear_combination heq
    exact (mul_eq_zero.mp hzero).resolve_left (sub_ne_zero.mpr hne)
  · intro h k hk
    rw [← Finset.sum_eq_multiset_sum Finset.univ,
      ← Finset.sum_eq_multiset_sum Finset.univ]
    simp_rw [mul_pow]
    rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
    by_cases hdk : d ∣ k
    · rw [(hζ.pow_eq_one_iff_dvd k).mpr hdk, one_mul]
    · rw [h k hk hdk, mul_zero]

/-- **Finite affine cyclic moment-symmetry law.**  An `n`-point spectrum is invariant under
rotation `z ↦ c + ζ(z-c)` about an arbitrary center exactly when its centered power sums in
all nontrivial cyclic-character sectors vanish through the sharp Torelli threshold `n`. -/
theorem finiteAffineCyclicSpectrum_fixed_iff_firstCenteredCharacterMoments_vanish
    {n d : ℕ} (f : Fin n → ℂ) (c : ℂ) {ζ : ℂ} (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ d) :
    (univ.val.map f).map (fun z => c + ζ * (z - c)) = univ.val.map f ↔
      ∀ k, k ≤ n → ¬ d ∣ k → ∑ i, (f i - c) ^ k = 0 := by
  rw [← finiteCyclicScaling_fixed_iff_firstCharacterMoments_vanish
    (fun i => f i - c) hζ]
  constructor
  · intro hfixed
    have hm := congrArg (Multiset.map (fun z : ℂ => z - c)) hfixed
    simp only [Multiset.map_map, Function.comp_apply] at hm ⊢
    convert hm using 1
    apply Multiset.map_congr rfl
    intro i hi
    ring
  · intro hfixed
    have hm := congrArg (Multiset.map (fun z : ℂ => c + z)) hfixed
    simp only [Multiset.map_map, Function.comp_apply] at hm ⊢
    convert hm using 1
    apply Multiset.map_congr rfl
    intro i hi
    ring

end

/-! # Order of multivariate power series

We work with `MvPowerSeries σ R`, for `Semiring R`, and `w : σ → ℕ`.

## Weighted Order

- `MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder`: the weighted order of a multivariate power series,
  with respect to `w`, as an element of `ℕ∞`.

- `MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder_zero`: the weighted order of `0` is `0`.

- `MvPowerSeries.ne_zero_iff_weightedOrder_finite`: a multivariate power series is nonzero if
  and only if its weighted order is finite.

- `MvPowerSeries.exists_coeff_ne_zero_of_weightedOrder`: if the weighted order is finite,
  then there exists a nonzero coefficient of weight the weighted order.

- `MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder_le` : if a coefficient is nonzero, then the weighted order is at
  most the weight of that exponent.

- `MvPowerSeries.coeff_eq_zero_of_lt_weightedOrder`: all coefficients of weights strictly less
  than the weighted order vanish.

- `MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder_eq_top_iff`: the weighted order of `f` is `⊤` if and only if `f = 0`.

- `MvPowerSeries.nat_le_weightedOrder`: if all coefficients of weight `< n` vanish, then the
  weighted order is at least `n`.

- `MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder_eq_nat_iff`: the weighted order is some integer `n` iff there
  exists a nonzero coefficient of weight `n`, and all coefficients of strictly smaller weight
  vanish.

- `MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder_monomial`, `MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder_monomial_of_ne_zero`:
  the weighted order of a monomial, of a monomial with nonzero coefficient.

- `MvPowerSeries.min_weightedOrder_le_add`: the order of the sum of two multivariate power series
  is at least the minimum of their orders.

- `MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder_add_of_weightedOrder_ne`: the `weightedOrder` of the sum of two
  formal power series is the minimum of their orders if their orders differ.

- `MvPowerSeries.le_weightedOrder_mul`: the `weightedOrder` of the product of two formal power
  series is at least the sum of their orders.

- `MvPowerSeries.coeff_mul_left_one_sub_of_lt_weightedOrder`,
  `MvPowerSeries.coeff_mul_right_one_sub_of_lt_weightedOrder`: the coefficients of `f * (1 - g)`
  and `(1 - g) * f` in weights strictly less than the weighted order of `g`.

- `MvPowerSeries.coeff_mul_prod_one_sub_of_lt_weightedOrder`: the coefficients of
  `f * Π i in s, (1 - g i)`, in weights strictly less than the weighted orders of `g i`, for
  `i ∈ s`.

## Order

- `MvPowerSeries.order`: the weighted order, for `w = (1 : σ → ℕ)`.

- `MvPowerSeries.ne_zero_iff_order_finite`: `f` is nonzero iff its order is finite.

- `MvPowerSeries.order_eq_top_iff`: the order of `f` is infinite iff `f = 0`.

- `MvPowerSeries.exists_coeff_ne_zero_of_order`: if the order is finite, then there exists a
  nonzero coefficient of degree equal to the order.

- `MvPowerSeries.order_le` : if a coefficient of some degree is nonzero, then the order
  is at least that degree.

- `MvPowerSeries.nat_le_order`: if all coefficients of degree strictly smaller than some integer
  vanish, then the order is at least that integer.

- `MvPowerSeries.order_eq_nat_iff`:  the order of a power series is an integer `n` iff there exists
  a nonzero coefficient in that degree, and all coefficients below that degree vanish.

- `MvPowerSeries.order_monomial`, `MvPowerSeries.order_monomial_of_ne_zero`: the order of a
  monomial, with a nonzero coefficient

- `MvPowerSeries.min_order_le_add`: the order of a sum of two power series is at least the minimum
  of their orders.

- `MvPowerSeries.order_add_of_order_ne`: the order of a sum of two power series of distinct orders
  is the minimum of their orders.

- `MvPowerSeries.order_mul_ge`: the order of a product of two power series is at least the sum of
  their orders.

- `MvPowerSeries.coeff_mul_left_one_sub_of_lt_order`,
  `MvPowerSeries.coeff_mul_right_one_sub_of_lt_order`: the coefficients of `f * (1 - g)` and
  `(1 - g) * f` below the order of `g` coincide with that of `f`.

- `MvPowerSeries.coeff_mul_prod_one_sub_of_lt_order`: the coefficients of `f * Π i in s, (1 - g i)`
  coincide with that of `f` below the minimum of the orders of the `g i`, for `i ∈ s`.

## Homogeneous components

- `MvPowerSeries.weightedHomogeneousComponent`, `MvPowerSeries.homogeneousComponent`: the power
  series which is the sum of all monomials of given weighted degree, resp. degree.

NOTE:
Under `Finite σ`, one can use `Finsupp.finite_of_degree_le` and `Finsupp.finite_of_weight_le` to
show that they have finite support, hence correspond to `MvPolynomial`.

However, when `σ` is finite, this is not necessarily an `MvPolynomial`.

/-!
# Finite affine-dihedral spectral Torelli universality

For a finite complex spectrum and a real center, the full affine dihedral generator pair is
visible in one sharp finite packet of centered power sums. Conjugation closure is exactly reality
of the first cardinality-many centered moments, while invariance under a primitive affine rotation
is exactly vanishing in its nontrivial character sectors through the same threshold.
-/

open scoped BigOperators
open Finset

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

noncomputable section

/-- Translation by a conjugation-fixed center intertwines conjugation closure of a finite spectrum
with conjugation closure of its centered translate. -/
private theorem conjugationClosed_centered_iff
    {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → ℂ) (c : ℂ) (hc : (starRingEnd ℂ) c = c) :
    (univ.val.map f).map (starRingEnd ℂ) = univ.val.map f ↔
      (univ.val.map (fun i => f i - c)).map (starRingEnd ℂ) =
        univ.val.map (fun i => f i - c) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hm := congrArg (Multiset.map (fun z : ℂ => z - c)) h
    simpa only [Multiset.map_map, Function.comp_apply, map_sub, hc] using hm
  · intro h
    have hm := congrArg (Multiset.map (fun z : ℂ => z + c)) h
    simpa only [Multiset.map_map, Function.comp_apply, map_sub, map_add, hc,
      sub_add_cancel] using hm

/-- **Finite affine-dihedral spectral Torelli universality law.** Let `c` be a real center and
`ζ` a primitive `d`th root. An `n`-point complex spectrum is simultaneously closed under
conjugation and fixed by `z ↦ c + ζ(z-c)` exactly when its centered power sums through order `n`
are real and all those in nontrivial cyclic-character sectors vanish. The common threshold `n`
is the sharp finite power-sum Torelli threshold; no labelled orbit decomposition is required. -/
theorem finiteAffineDihedralSpectrum_fixed_iff_firstCenteredDihedralMoments
    {n d : ℕ} (f : Fin n → ℂ) (c : ℂ) (hc : (starRingEnd ℂ) c = c)
    {ζ : ℂ} (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ d) :
    ((univ.val.map f).map (starRingEnd ℂ) = univ.val.map f ∧
        (univ.val.map f).map (fun z => c + ζ * (z - c)) = univ.val.map f) ↔
      (∀ k, k ≤ n →
        (starRingEnd ℂ) (∑ i, (f i - c) ^ k) = ∑ i, (f i - c) ^ k) ∧
      (∀ k, k ≤ n → ¬ d ∣ k → ∑ i, (f i - c) ^ k = 0) := by
  rw [conjugationClosed_centered_iff f c hc]
  rw [finiteSatake_conjugationClosed_iff_firstMoments_real
    (fun i => f i - c)]
  rw [finiteAffineCyclicSpectrum_fixed_iff_firstCenteredCharacterMoments_vanish
    f c hζ]
  simp only [Finset.sum_eq_multiset_sum Finset.univ]

end

end GaloisForLFunctions

import Mathlib

/-!
# A nonzero polynomial is nonzero along an injective sequence infinitely often

A nonzero polynomial has finitely many roots, so along an injective sequence `b` its value
`Q(b M)` vanishes for only finitely many `M`.  Hence on any infinite index set there is an `M`
at which `Q(b M) ≠ 0` (`exists_mem_eval_ne_zero`).

For the leading symbol of a homogeneous differential polynomial evaluated at the exponent
sequence, this selects a scale at which the leading-symbol combination does not vanish — while
staying inside the infinite set of scales where the series coefficient is nonzero.
-/

open Polynomial

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

/-- **Eval selector.**  A nonzero polynomial, composed with an injective sequence, is nonzero
at some index of any infinite index set. -/
theorem exists_mem_eval_ne_zero {b : ℕ → ℂ} (hb : Function.Injective b) {Q : Polynomial ℂ}
    (hQ : Q ≠ 0) {s : Set ℕ} (hs : s.Infinite) : ∃ M ∈ s, Q.eval (b M) ≠ 0 := by
  have h1 : {x : ℂ | Q.eval x = 0}.Finite := by
    apply Set.Finite.subset Q.roots.toFinset.finite_toSet
    intro x hx
    exact Multiset.mem_toFinset.mpr (Polynomial.mem_roots'.mpr ⟨hQ, hx⟩)
  have hfin : {M | Q.eval (b M) = 0}.Finite :=
    (h1.preimage hb.injOn).subset (fun M hM => hM)
  obtain ⟨M, hMs, hM0⟩ := (hs.sdiff hfin).nonempty
  exact ⟨M, hMs, hM0⟩

end GaloisForLFunctions
